panels.description: Product name from NVML.
panels.title: Device

panels.description: Share of the last NVML sample window with a kernel running.
panels.title: GPU busy

panels.description: 1 when the kprobes are attached.
panels.title: Probe

panels.description: 1 when the shared worker answered the scrape.
panels.title: Sampler

panels.description: NVML's device utilization, and the per-process SM time NVML attributes summed over processes. The two should agree under a single workload.

targets.legendFormat: gpu {{gpu}} SM time, from process samples

panels.title: GPU utilization

panels.description: Derivative of the energy counter; should track power draw.
panels.title: Energy rate

panels.description: Each clock domain as a share of the highest clock it can reach. Below 1 under load means something is holding it down; see the throttle panel for why.
panels.title: Clock vs ceiling

panels.description: Current clock of each domain. Graphics and SM idle in the low hundreds of MHz and jump to the ceiling under load.
panels.title: Clocks

panels.description: Why the driver is holding the clocks down, one lane per reason: idle, power cap, thermal, hardware brake, application clock settings. Red means active.
panels.title: Throttle reasons

panels.description: P-state as a number: 0 is P0, flat out; 8 and above is idle. A card stuck above P0 under load is being throttled.
panels.title: Performance state

panels.description: Generation the link is running at against what the card and slot support. The link drops to gen 1 when the card idles and should renegotiate up under load; stuck low means a slot or riser problem.
panels.title: PCIe link

panels.description: Bytes moving over the link, tx out of the card and rx into it, over NVML's sample window.
panels.title: PCIe throughput

panels.description: Board draw against the enforced cap and the most the card accepts. Draw pinned at the enforced line is a power cap throttle.
panels.title: Power vs limits

panels.description: Memory in use and reserved by the driver against the total. Compare with the per-process panel below to see who holds it.
panels.title: Device memory

panels.description: Share of the window the memory controller was busy next to the share a kernel was running. Memory high with SM low is a bandwidth-bound workload.
panels.title: Memory controller vs SM busy

panels.description: PCIe replays per second and ECC error counts. ECC rows are absent on cards without it; any rise here is a hardware problem.
panels.title: Link and memory errors

panels.description: CPU time rate of each process holding a GPU context; 1 = one core.
panels.title: Host CPU by process

panels.description: One row per NVML context right now.
panels.title: Contexts

panels.description: ioctl calls into /dev/nvidia* and /dev/nvidiactl, by thread name.
panels.title: Resource manager ioctls by process

panels.description: ioctl calls into /dev/nvidia-uvm, by thread name.
panels.title: Unified memory ioctls by process

panels.description: Every DRM driver; cardN is KMS, renderDN is render.
panels.title: DRM ioctls by node

panels.description: Seconds per ioctl, kretprobe minus kprobe, per thread name.
panels.title: Mean time inside the driver

panels.description: Share of wall time threads spend inside driver ioctls; 1 = one thread always in the driver.
panels.title: Time inside the driver

panels.description: rm_control is the hot path for everything; rm_alloc and rm_map_memory are setup.
panels.title: Resource manager ioctls by escape

panels.description: nvidiactl is the control node every client opens; nvidiaN is the GPU itself.
panels.title: Resource manager ioctls by node

panels.description: Per-pid totals for pids the probes saw in the last 5 minutes.
panels.title: Recent pids touching the driver

panels.description: Open fds on /dev/nvidia* and /dev/dri/*, with or without an NVML context.
panels.title: Processes holding a node

panels.description: A reset means the keeper or the worker restarted and the kernel counters started over.
panels.title: Sampler uptime
